title.title: Anticanonical nonvanishing in every dimension
title.subtitle: Claim: if $-K_X$ carries a smooth semipositive metric, some power $-mK_X$ has a section

plain: If a shape's anti-curvature is never negative, it has at least one 'anti-canonical' section somewhere

object.heading: The main theorem and the papers it rests on (schematic)

beats.text: Seven papers form one chain; several are stated reductions
The structure theorem splits the universal cover; torus actions are the hard part

steps: Known theorems split the space into flat, Ricci-flat and rational parts
The hard part carries a torus action
Count invariant sections with an Euler characteristic: one exists

achievement.label: Yau's problem: anticanonical nonvanishing
achievement.context: Before: structure theorems (Cao–Höring 2019); for merely nef $-K_X$ it is false
achievement.note: Seven manuscripts, 270 pages, several of them reductions

verify.detail: No Lean; the whole chain is paper-only
verify.ourCheck: We read the claim and caveats; we did not check the proof

voice.text: If minus K carries a semipositive metric, must some power have a section?
Split the cover, then count torus-invariant sections using an Euler characteristic.
Claimed: yes, for every smooth complex projective variety.

sources.quote: Nonvanishing for nef −K is false in general
